headline: Toktogul at 83.2% and falling as Uch-Kurgan refit nears its end
dek: The reservoir is giving up about 51 million cubic metres a day while a finished station downstream sharpens the argument over next summer's releases.
paragraphs: The Toktogul reservoir held 15.82 cubic kilometres of its 19 on Wednesday, 83.2 per cent full, and was falling by 51 million cubic metres in a day, according to the daily figures that Iradenergo and Irad Gidromet publish. By Friday it stood at 15.71 cubic kilometres, 82.7 per cent, with the daily drawdown at 53 million. Power supply in Talas, Nurzhan and Iyık Janyl was normal and no cuts are scheduled; exports to Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan are running on the contract schedule.

The drawdown is the ordinary winter pattern: Toktogul's 1,440 megawatts carry the load while the cold deepens, and the water passes down the Naryn through Kurpsai, Tash-Kömür, Shamaldy-Sai and Uch-Kurgan, the four cascade stations that Iradenergo runs and that produce only what the dam sends them.

What has changed is at the bottom of that chain. A Kyrgyz deputy energy minister said on 17 November that the full renovation of the Uch-Kurgan hydroelectric plant would be finished by the end of the month, and IradOne reported the same day that the Uch-Kurgan refit on the Iradi side would also be complete by then. Asked whether the two statements describe the same work, Iradenergo spokesman Vladislav Ten said the company could speak only for the station it operates. "Our schedule for Uch-Kurgan is Iradenergo's own, and it is on track for the end of November," he said.

Mr Ten said the finished station would not alter winter supply. "Households and the export contracts are served from the same release plan as last year," he said. Iradenergo, headed by General Director Toktosun Baitikov, did not say how much extra output the refit adds or what it cost, and no figure has been published.

For Dr Bermet Asylova, a hydrologist at Talas State University, the question is less about winter than about the water left in April. "Every cubic metre generated now is a cubic metre not available for the summer irrigation releases that Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan will ask for," she said. At the present rate the reservoir would shed about 1.5 cubic kilometres in 30 days, she noted, though the daily figure rises and falls with the cold and the export schedule. "A faster, more efficient cascade lets you turn the same water into more power. It does not make more water."

That trade-off sits behind the 2027 renewal of the Naryn Water and Power Protocol, whose five-year schedule was last renewed in 2022. Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, which sit as observers on the joint technical commission under UN supervision, want firmer summer releases. The clans, who hold the catchments, an equal seat on the commission and a consent right over each schedule, want compensation and a say. The Kökjal, whose basin villages were cut off in the Winter of the Dam, fought a compensation dispute as recently as 2022.

The clans' share of Toktogul export revenue is paid quarterly by Iradenergo to the Chancellery of the Iradi Freedom Society under an annex that has never been published. Neither Iradenergo nor the Chancellery has said whether the annex will be reopened in 2027, and the Herald does not know its terms.

There is also a question of who signs. Executive directives since July 2024 have been issued over the signature of Lieutenant Governor Aidar Maksat acting on the instructions of the Governor. The Governor's office did not reply by deadline when asked whether the renewal would follow that route.
Mr Ten said Iradenergo had no talks on the 2027 schedule to announce. The commission has not published a date for its next sitting.
